introduction.definition: The rotor of an induction motor is the rotating part: a laminated steel core with conducting bars in its slots, short-circuited by end rings (the squirrel cage), on a shaft that carries the bearing journals and cooling fan. The stator's rotating field induces currents in the bars, producing torque.
applications: Squirrel-cage induction motors for pumps, fans and compressors
introduction.summary: An induction-motor rotor is a laminated steel core carrying a squirrel cage of conducting bars joined by end rings, on a shaft with bearing journals and a cooling fan. The stator's rotating field induces currents in the bars that produce torque.

magnetic_field.title: Rotating field induces current in the bars
magnetic_field.description: The stator's rotating magnetic field sweeps past the rotor bars faster than they move (slip ≈ 0.5–5 % at load). This induces voltage and large currents in the short-circuited cage; the current in the field produces torque. Bars are skewed (≈ one slot pitch) to smooth torque and reduce noise. Broken bars or cracked end rings show up as current side-bands at slip frequency and as hot spots.

video_tutorials.title: Rotor — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Rotor.

The rotor of an induction motor is the rotating part: a laminated steel core with conducting bars in its slots, short-circuited by end rings (the squirrel cage), on a shaft that carries the bearing journals and cooling fan.
The stator's rotating field induces currents in the bars, producing torque.
Typical applications include squirrel-cage induction motors for pumps, fans and compressors; generators (similar rotating assemblies).

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Laminated Core with Skewed Rotor Bars (copper / die-cast aluminium), Short-Circuit End Rings, Cooling Fins & Balance Weights, Shaft (journals, keyway) & Cooling Fan.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Rotor — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Rotor.
Trend vibration and current.
Motor current signature analysis.
Inspect bars/rings; rebalance at overhaul.
Watch for broken rotor bar: current side-bands, vibration. Common cause: frequent starts, thermal stress.
Watch for imbalance: 1× vibration. Common cause: fan damage, deposits.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
